newsitem.title: USA: Edison Calif. nuke at 56 pct and rising.
newsitem.headline: Edison Calif. nuke at 56 pct and rising.

text.p: Unit 3 at the San Onofre nuclear plant near San Clemente, Calif., is operating at 56 percent and should reach full power in about 20 hours, a spokesman for Edison International's Southern California Edison Co said early Friday.
The 1,080-megawatt (MW) unit was brought down to 46 percent power Thursday evening after a control rod, one of 91 in the unit, was inadvertently dropped, said spokesman Ray Golden.
Operators were able to retrieve the rod, which apparently fell when a cooling fan was disconnected and electronic components were allowed to overheat, he added.
The unit is ramping up at a rate of about 3 percent an hour, said Golden.
San Onofre's 1,070 MW unit 2 is scheduled to shut November 30 for a 70-day refueling outage.
Edison has a 75 percent stake in the San Onofre units, while San Diego Gas and Electric Co, a subsidiary of Enova Corp, owns 20 percent and two municipal utilities own the remaining five percent.
